differences.what: Actual master reviewed: pointed north cone and lower connector retain the integrated flat north facade and curved west drum. The corrected north service door/window and stable roof junction remain visible.

T-2228 cupola body: the dovecote body now stands clear of the stable ridge with both pigeon-hole tiers in open air, and the pyramid rises well above the north gable apex as the photograph shows (body top 41.0, apex 47.0 ft ng, from 38.9/43.3). Read against the gable apex and ridge crest: apex about 35 px over the gable apex against the photograph's 45 (within the +/-1 ft bound), pyramid slope apex-to-SW-eave 60,73 px against 58,82.

Stable cupola and opening/ornament correspondence still differ in the unchanged camera. Retain these in the final audit. The stable end of this side-by-side sits about 28 px off because this whole-house camera is fitted at the Prairie corner (T-2758, the item after this).

T-2228: the cupola centre reads about 22 px (roughly 4 ft by parallax) north of the owner-directed S14.6, kept; the whole stable roof reads about 28 px low in this camera, which is camera/height uncertainty, not yet a roof correction. T-2758: it is the camera, not the roof. This camera's only vertical controls are the grade and eave at the Prairie corner (W 0), 141 ft east of the stable, so at the stable it draws 14.6 px a foot where the carriage doorway (sheet 2 jambs W 134.9-147.0, sheet 5 soffit 12.6 ft) measures 13.85 in the print. Re-solved with the doorway's four corners added (eye height or image lean free in turn), it reads the gable's coping apex at 38.1-38.6 ft and the cupola's apex at 45.5-46.3 ft on the model's centre (model 39.6 and 47.0), and the doorway as a bare ruler reads the coping apex at 38.8 ft. The residual of about 1 ft is inside the ridge's 1.5 ft tolerance and is no larger than the Cornell view's re-solved disagreement with it (38.3-39.5 ft), so the roof is not changed. The 4 ft parallax was not a reading: every control in this photograph lies in the north face, so its depth is free: with the pixel aspect let go, which those controls cannot measure, fits of one RMS (3.9 px) slide the cupola from S14.4 at square pixels to S10.4 at an aspect of 1.06 while the gable's height does not move. The Cornell view, re-solved on two faces, puts it at S13.0-13.2, about 1.5 ft north of S14.6, which does not hold up as a question for the owner. The doorway re-solve is not adopted here: it moves the north tower's finial about 9 px off the print where this camera holds it to 1.5 px, so one level pinhole does not fit both ends of this print. data/comparisons/glessner/stable-roof-heights.json (tools/glessner_stable_roof_read.py).

The later overhead garage door, closed loft opening, vehicles, utilities and surrounding1963 street fabric are not carried back as1904 details. This crop alone does not establish exact original color.

T-2848 light: the render now takes the photograph's own sun, low from the east-north-east (camera solve.light), so the 18th Street wall is raked from the left and the stable's west end falls in shade as in the print; it no longer uses the review default. The elevation is a plausible summer-morning height, not a measured shadow length.
T-2848: the stone in this print is darkened by decades of city soot, so its tone in the 1960s photograph is not its 1887 tone; the render's clean stone is not compared against it.
